Lewes non-profits by government grant revenue in 2024: Lewes Fire Department Inc leads city ranking
E. W. Hare
Lewes, Delaware non-profits in 2024 were led by Lewes Fire Department Inc, which reported $2,693,498 in government grant revenue and $5,759,822 in total revenue in its IRS Form 990 filing. Government grants made up 46.8% of its reported total revenue.
The ranking reflects non-profits with available Form 990-series government grant revenue data that met the ranking's data criteria and may not include every non-profit in the city.
The ranking is based on IRS Form 990 filings, the annual information returns most tax-exempt organizations file with the IRS. The form includes reported revenue, expenses, assets, governance information and compensation paid to certain people, making it a public source for comparing large tax-exempt organizations' finances.
The figures reflect what each organization reported for its filing year, including total revenue, contributions, government grants, compensation, the number of employees and assets at the start and end of the year. Because nonprofits can differ by mission, structure and accounting period, the totals are best read as reported financial measures, not as a direct measure of local charitable activity.
Among the 8 ranked organizations with calculable government-grant shares, the median share of reported total revenue from government grants was 29.1%. The organization with the highest share of revenue from government grants was What Is Your Voice Inc, at 52.4%.
Lewes Fire Department Inc reported an increase in government grant revenue from $2,384,817 in the prior year to $2,693,498, up $308,681, or 12.9%. The Greater Lewes Foundation also saw its government grant revenue rise from $292,426 to $1,243,999, an increase of $951,573, or 325.4%.
Lewes Fire Department Inc reported total contributions of $3,685,430, of which $991,932 was categorized as all other contributions. Over the year, its asset balances rose from $13,069,046 at the beginning to $14,558,240 at the end, an increase of 11.4%.
Tax-exempt organizations include a wide range of groups, such as charities, foundations, educational institutions and other mission-driven organizations. Under IRS rules, 501(c)(3) organizations must be organized and operated for exempt purposes, and their earnings cannot benefit private shareholders or individuals.
